classification.difficultyReason: Students use the isosceles triangle's bisected base in the explicitly requested Pythagoras calculation, then use that height to find prism volume and subtract the cylindrical hole using its diameter.

content.prompt: Consider this isosceles triangular prism with a hole through the middle.

spec.description: Isosceles triangular prism with a circular bore. Front opening is solid, rear opening and longitudinal bore edges are dashed. The bore diameter has two arrowheads and a centre point. Ordinary source blue linework is rendered black.
spec.mathematics: Triangular base 20 cm, equal sloping sides 26 cm, perpendicular height y, prism length 60 cm and circular bore diameter 9 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: The height y is unknown; no calculated height or volume is inserted.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular height bisects the 20 cm base because the triangle is isosceles.
$$\begin{align*}y^2+10^2&=26^2\\y^2&=676-100=576\\y&=\sqrt{576}=24\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence, show the volume is approximately $10\,583\text{ cm}^3$.

answer.worked:
The hole has radius $9\div2=4.5\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{prism}}&=\left(\frac12\times20\times24\right)\times60=14\,400\text{ cm}^3\\V_{\text{hole}}&=\pi(4.5)^2\times60=1215\pi\text{ cm}^3\\V&=14\,400-1215\pi\text{ cm}^3\\V&\approx10\,583\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$
